description: SAT Math questions covering ratios, percentages, statistics, probability, and data interpretation

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A recipe calls for 2 cups of flour to make 24 cookies. How many cups of flour are needed to make 60 cookies?
questions.explanation: Set up proportion: 2/24 = x/60. Cross multiply: 24x = 120, so x = 5 cups.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A shirt originally costs $50. If it is on sale for 20% off, what is the sale price?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the median of the data set: 3, 7, 9, 12, 15?
questions.explanation: The data is already sorted. With 5 values, the median is the middle (3rd) value: 9.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A bag contains 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. If one marble is selected at random, what is the probability it is red?
questions.explanation: Total marbles = 4 + 6 = 10. P(red) = 4/10 = 2/5.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: If a car travels 150 miles in 3 hours, what is its average speed in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance/time = 150/3 = 50 mph.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: What is 15% of 80?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the mean of: 4, 8, 12, 16?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: The line of best fit for a data set is y = 3x + 5. What is the predicted y-value when x = 4?

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A fair coin is flipped twice. What is the probability of getting heads both times?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:4. If there are 12 boys, how many girls are there?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A map has a scale of 1 inch = 50 miles. If two cities are 4 inches apart on the map, what is the actual distance?
questions.explanation: Distance = 4 × 50 = 200 miles.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A $60 item is marked down by 10%. What is the new price?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the range of the data set: 5, 12, 8, 3, 15?
questions.explanation: Range = maximum - minimum = 15 - 3 = 12.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A scatterplot shows points that generally go up from left to right. This indicates:
questions.explanation: Points going up from left to right indicate a positive correlation (as x increases, y increases).

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6. P = 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: If 5 apples cost $3, how much do 15 apples cost?
questions.explanation: 5 apples : $3 = 15 apples : x. Since 15 = 3 × 5, x = 3 × $3 = $9.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: What percent of 50 is 10?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the median of: 2, 5, 7, 9, 10, 15?
questions.explanation: With 6 values, median is average of 3rd and 4th values: (7 + 9)/2 = 8.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A jar has 3 red, 5 blue, and 2 green candies. What is the probability of picking a blue candy?
questions.explanation: Total = 10 candies. P(blue) = 5/10 = 1/2.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: If a line of best fit has equation y = 2x + 10, what is y when x = 0?
questions.explanation: When x = 0, y = 2(0) + 10 = 10. This is the y-intercept.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A printer prints 30 pages in 5 minutes. How many pages can it print in 12 minutes?
questions.explanation: Rate = 30/5 = 6 pages/min. In 12 minutes: 6 × 12 = 72 pages.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: If 25% of a number is 15, what is the number?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Five students scored 80, 85, 85, 90, and 95 on a test. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. 85 appears twice; others appear once.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: What is the probability of drawing a heart from a standard deck of 52 cards?
questions.explanation: There are 13 hearts in a deck of 52. P = 13/52 = 1/4.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A car uses 2 gallons of gas to travel 50 miles. How many gallons are needed for 200 miles?

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A store sells an item for $80, which is 25% more than the cost. What was the cost?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: The sum of 5 numbers is 75. What is the mean?
questions.explanation: Mean = sum/count = 75/5 = 15.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: In the equation y = -0.5x + 100, what does -0.5 represent?
questions.explanation: In y = mx + b form, m (-0.5) is the slope, representing the rate of change.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1-8. What is the probability of spinning an even number?
questions.explanation: Even numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8 (4 numbers). P = 4/8 = 1/2.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: If 3 workers can complete a job in 6 days, how many days would it take 6 workers?
questions.explanation: Work is inversely proportional to workers. 3 × 6 = 6 × x → x = 3 days.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A store increases the price of a jacket by 20%, then decreases the new price by 20%. If the original price was $100, what is the final price?
questions.explanation: After 20% increase: $100 × 1.20 = $120. After 20% decrease: $120 × 0.80 = $96.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: The test scores 72, 78, 82, 85, 85, 88, 90, 92, 98 have what mode?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. 85 appears twice; all others appear once. Mode = 85.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A scatterplot shows a strong negative correlation. Which statement is true?
questions.choice_c: x and y are not related
questions.choice_d: y is always greater than x
questions.explanation: Negative correlation means as one variable increases, the other decreases.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A bag has 3 red, 4 blue, and 5 green marbles. What is the probability of NOT drawing a green marble?
questions.explanation: Total = 12. Not green = 3 + 4 = 7. P(not green) = 7/12.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: A poll of 500 voters shows 52% support a candidate with a margin of error of ±3%. Which range represents the likely percentage of all voters who support the candidate?
questions.explanation: 52% ± 3% gives a range of 49% to 55%.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A car uses 8 gallons of gas to travel 240 miles. At this rate, how many gallons are needed to travel 420 miles?
questions.explanation: Rate = 240/8 = 30 miles per gallon. Gallons needed = 420/30 = 14.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: If a population increases from 800 to 1000, what is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = 1000 - 800 = 200. Percent increase = (200/800) × 100 = 25%.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: The range of a data set is 24 and the minimum value is 17. What is the maximum value?
questions.explanation: Range = max - min. So 24 = max - 17 → max = 41.

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A study finds that students who eat breakfast score higher on tests. This is best described as:
questions.choice_c: Proof that breakfast causes higher scores
questions.explanation: Since researchers observed existing behavior without assigning treatments, this is an observational study. It shows correlation, not causation.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A train travels 240 km in 3 hours. A car travels the same distance in 4 hours. How much faster is the train than the car (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: Train speed = 240/3 = 80 km/h. Car speed = 240/4 = 60 km/h. Difference = 20 km/h.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A population decreased from 5000 to 4500. What was the percent decrease?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A data set has mean 20 and 10 values. If a new value of 30 is added, what is the new mean?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A line of best fit has equation y = 50 - 2x. If x increases by 10, what happens to y?
questions.explanation: The slope is -2, meaning for each unit increase in x, y decreases by 2. For 10 units, y decreases by 20.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability it is a face card (J, Q, K)?
questions.explanation: There are 12 face cards (3 per suit × 4 suits). P = 12/52 = 3/13.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: A survey of 400 people has a margin of error of ±5%. If 200 supported a proposal, what is the confidence interval?
questions.explanation: Sample proportion = 200/400 = 50%. Interval = 50% ± 5% = 45% to 55%.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A faucet fills a tank in 4 hours. A drain empties it in 6 hours. If both are open, how long to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Rate in = 1/4 tank/hr, rate out = 1/6 tank/hr. Net rate = 1/4 - 1/6 = 3/12 - 2/12 = 1/12 tank/hr. Time = 12 hours.

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: Which sampling method is most likely to result in bias?
questions.choice_a: Random selection from a complete list
questions.choice_c: Surveying only people at a shopping mall
questions.explanation: Surveying only at a mall introduces selection bias since it excludes people who don't shop there.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: An item's price increased by 50%, then increased by 20%. What is the total percent increase from the original?
questions.explanation: After 50% increase: 1.50. After 20% increase: 1.50 × 1.20 = 1.80. Total increase = 80%.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: If the mean of 6 numbers is 15, and one number is removed and the new mean is 16, what was the removed number?
questions.explanation: Original sum = 6 × 15 = 90. New sum = 5 × 16 = 80. Removed number = 90 - 80 = 10.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.explanation: Outcomes with 2 heads: HHT, HTH, THH = 3. Total outcomes = 8. P = 3/8.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: The correlation coefficient between study hours and test scores is r = 0.8. This means:
questions.explanation: r = 0.8 indicates a strong positive correlation (close to 1).

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A solution is 30% acid. How much pure water must be added to 10 liters to make it 20% acid?
questions.explanation: Acid amount = 3 liters. After adding water: 3/(10 + x) = 0.20 → 3 = 2 + 0.2x → x = 5 liters.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: Which would most likely decrease the margin of error in a survey?
questions.explanation: Margin of error is inversely related to the square root of sample size. Larger samples give smaller margins.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Which measure of center is most affected by outliers?
questions.explanation: The mean is most sensitive to extreme values (outliers) because it uses all values in its calculation.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A shirt is marked down 40% to $36. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: 60% of original = $36. Original = 36/0.60 = $60.

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A study randomly assigns some plants to receive fertilizer and others to receive none. This is:
questions.explanation: Random assignment of treatments to subjects makes this a randomized experiment.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: If P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3, and A and B are independent, what is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.12.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: The equation C = 25 + 0.15m models the cost of a rental car where m is miles driven. What does 25 represent?
questions.explanation: The constant 25 is the cost when m = 0, representing the base rental fee.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A recipe for 8 servings uses 3 cups of rice. How many cups are needed for 12 servings?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A dataset has mean 50 and standard deviation 10. If each value is multiplied by 2 then 5 is added, what is the new mean?
questions.explanation: New mean = 2(old mean) + 5 = 2(50) + 5 = 105.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: A researcher wants to reduce the margin of error by half. What should she do to the sample size?
questions.explanation: Margin of error is inversely proportional to √n. To halve margin of error, multiply sample size by 4 (since √4 = 2).

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: In a class, 60% are female. Of females, 25% play sports. Of males, 40% play sports. What percentage of the class plays sports?
questions.explanation: Females playing sports: 0.60 × 0.25 = 0.15 (15%). Males playing sports: 0.40 × 0.40 = 0.16 (16%). Total: 15% + 16% = 31%.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: The equation y = 2.5x + 15 models monthly costs y (dollars) based on usage x (hours). What does 15 represent?
questions.explanation: In y = mx + b form, b (the y-intercept) represents the cost when x = 0, i.e., the fixed monthly fee.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: After a 15% discount, an item costs $68. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: If 85% of original = $68, then original = 68/0.85 = $80.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Adding which value to {10, 15, 20, 25, 30} would most increase the standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures spread. Adding 50 (far from the mean of 20) increases spread the most.

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A study randomly assigns participants to either receive a new medication or a placebo. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Random assignment to treatment groups (medication vs placebo) is the hallmark of a randomized controlled experiment.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Machine A produces 100 widgets in 4 hours. Machine B produces 150 widgets in 5 hours. Working together, how many widgets can they produce in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Rate A = 100/4 = 25/hr. Rate B = 150/5 = 30/hr. Combined rate = 55/hr. In 2 hours: 55 × 2 = 110 widgets.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A test is 90% accurate. If 5% of the population has a disease, what is the probability a person who tests positive actually has the disease? (Assume test accuracy applies to both positives and negatives.)
questions.explanation: Using Bayes: P(disease|positive) = P(positive|disease)×P(disease) / P(positive). P(positive) = 0.9×0.05 + 0.1×0.95 = 0.045 + 0.095 = 0.14. Result = 0.045/0.14 ≈ 0.32 or 32%.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A scatterplot shows study hours (x) vs test scores (y). The correlation coefficient is r = 0.85. What percent of the variation in test scores is explained by study hours?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of determination r² = 0.85² = 0.7225 = 72.25% explains the variation.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A car traveling at 60 mph is 30 miles behind a car traveling at 50 mph. How long until the first car catches up?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 60 - 50 = 10 mph. Time to close 30-mile gap = 30/10 = 3 hours.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: An investment grows 20% the first year and loses 10% the second year. What is the overall percent change?
questions.explanation: After year 1: 1.20. After year 2: 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08. Overall change = 8% increase.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: In a dataset, the mean is 50 and standard deviation is 10. If each value is transformed by the rule y = 2x - 20, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is affected by multiplication but not addition. New SD = 2 × 10 = 20.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: Two cards are drawn without replacement from a standard deck. What is the probability both are aces?
questions.explanation: P(first ace) = 4/52. P(second ace | first ace) = 3/51. P(both) = (4/52)(3/51) = 12/2652 = 1/221.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: A sample of 100 has margin of error 10%. What sample size would give margin of error 5%?
questions.explanation: Margin of error ∝ 1/√n. To halve margin, quadruple n: 100 × 4 = 400.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A regression model gives y = 0.8x + 5. If the residual for x = 10 is -2, what is the actual y-value?
questions.explanation: Predicted: y = 0.8(10) + 5 = 13. Residual = actual - predicted = -2. Actual = 13 - 2 = 11.

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A study finds people who exercise have lower stress. Which statement is most accurate?
questions.choice_b: Lower stress causes people to exercise
questions.choice_c: There is an association between exercise and stress
questions.explanation: Observational studies show association/correlation, not causation. We can only say there's an association.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A mixture is 40% alcohol. How much pure alcohol must be added to 100 mL to make it 60% alcohol?
questions.explanation: Current alcohol: 40 mL. After adding x mL: (40 + x)/(100 + x) = 0.60. 40 + x = 60 + 0.6x. 0.4x = 20. x = 50 mL.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: The population grew 25% over 5 years. What was the average annual percent growth rate (compound)?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: The five-number summary of a data set is: Min=10, Q1=25, Med=35, Q3=50, Max=80. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: If P(A|B) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.5, what is P(A and B)?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A linear model predicts sales. The residual plot shows a clear curved pattern. This suggests:
questions.choice_b: A nonlinear model may be better
questions.explanation: A pattern in the residual plot suggests the linear model doesn't capture the relationship well; a nonlinear model may be better.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: Two polls show 52% and 48% support with margins of error ±4% and ±3% respectively. Can we conclude the first has more support?
questions.choice_b: No, because the confidence intervals overlap
questions.choice_c: Yes, because both margins are small
questions.explanation: First: 48%-56%. Second: 45%-51%. The intervals overlap (48%-51%), so we cannot conclude a significant difference.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A and B together complete a job in 6 days. A alone takes 10 days. How long does B take alone?

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A drug trial uses double-blind methodology. This means:
questions.choice_b: Neither participants nor researchers know who receives treatment
questions.explanation: Double-blind means neither the participants nor the researchers administering the treatment know who is in the treatment vs. control group.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A quantity decreases by 20% and then increases by what percent to return to its original value?
questions.explanation: After 20% decrease: 0.80. To return to 1.00: 1.00/0.80 = 1.25, which is a 25% increase.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A data set has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Using the empirical rule, about what percent of data falls between 70 and 130?
questions.explanation: 70 to 130 is 100 ± 30 = 100 ± 2(15), which is 2 standard deviations. About 95% falls within 2 SD.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: In a group, 70% like coffee, 50% like tea, and 30% like both. What percent like coffee or tea?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: An exponential model y = 100(1.05)^x fits data well. What is the percent growth rate per unit of x?
questions.explanation: In y = a(1 + r)^x form, r = 0.05 = 5% growth rate.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Walking at 4 mph, a trip takes 30 minutes longer than biking at 12 mph. How far is the trip?
questions.explanation: Let d = distance. Time walking = d/4, biking = d/12. d/4 - d/12 = 0.5 hours. 3d/12 - d/12 = 0.5. 2d/12 = 0.5. d = 3 miles.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A map has a scale of 1 inch = 20 miles. If two cities are 3 inches apart on the map, what is the actual distance?
questions.explanation: 3 inches × 20 miles/inch = 60 miles.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A shirt originally costs $40. It is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Discount = 25% of $40 = $10. Sale price = $40 - $10 = $30.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the mean of the data set: 4, 7, 9, 12, 8?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the median of: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11?
questions.explanation: The middle value of the ordered list is 7.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A bag contains 3 red and 7 blue marbles. What is the probability of picking a red marble?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: If 5 apples cost $3, how much do 15 apples cost?
questions.explanation: 15 apples = 3 × 5 apples, so cost = 3 × $3 = $9.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: What is 15% of 80?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the range of: 10, 15, 8, 22, 17?
questions.explanation: Range = maximum - minimum = 22 - 8 = 14.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A fair coin is flipped. What is the probability of getting heads?
questions.explanation: A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes, so P(heads) = 1/2.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A recipe calls for 2 cups of flour for 24 cookies. How many cups are needed for 36 cookies?
questions.explanation: 36/24 = 1.5 times the recipe. Flour = 2 × 1.5 = 3 cups.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A store marks up items by 50%. If an item costs $20 wholesale, what is the retail price?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the mode of: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 3, 6?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. 3 appears three times.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A die is rolled. What is the probability of getting an even number?
questions.explanation: Even numbers: 2, 4, 6. P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance/time = 150/3 = 50 mph.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: If a number increases from 50 to 60, what is the percent increase?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: The median of 8 ordered numbers is 15. What must be true?
questions.choice_b: The average of 4th and 5th numbers is 15
questions.explanation: For even-sized data, median is the average of the two middle values (4th and 5th).

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: If P(A) = 0.4 and A and B are mutually exclusive with P(B) = 0.3, what is P(A or B)?
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:2. If there are 12 boys, how many girls are there?
questions.explanation: 3:2 = 12:x. Cross multiply: 3x = 24, x = 8 girls.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: Express 3/4 as a percentage.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A scatterplot shows points forming an upward pattern from left to right. This indicates:
questions.explanation: An upward pattern indicates positive correlation: as x increases, y increases.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Convert 2.5 hours to minutes.
questions.explanation: 2.5 hours × 60 minutes/hour = 150 minutes.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A student scored 45 out of 50 on a test. What percentage is this?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Which measure of center is most affected by outliers?
questions.explanation: The mean is affected by all values including outliers; median is more resistant.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4 when rolling a fair die?
questions.explanation: Numbers greater than 4: 5, 6. P = 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: If 3 workers can complete a job in 6 hours, how long would 6 workers take?
questions.explanation: Work is inversely proportional to workers. 6 workers = double the workers, half the time = 3 hours.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: What is 100% of 75?
questions.explanation: 100% of any number equals the number itself: 100% of 75 = 75.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: If a line of best fit has equation y = 2x + 5, what is the predicted y when x = 3?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A data set has values 5, 5, 5, 5, 5. What is the standard deviation?
questions.explanation: All values are identical, so there is no spread. Standard deviation = 0.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: If two events cannot occur at the same time, they are called:
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot happen simultaneously.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A printer prints 30 pages in 5 minutes. How many pages per minute?
questions.explanation: Rate = 30 pages / 5 minutes = 6 pages per minute.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A car uses 8 gallons of gas to travel 240 miles. At this rate, how many gallons are needed for 360 miles?
questions.explanation: Rate = 240/8 = 30 miles/gallon. Gallons needed = 360/30 = 12.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A price increases by 20% then decreases by 20%. What is the net change from the original?
questions.explanation: Let original = 100. After +20%: 120. After -20%: 120 × 0.8 = 96. Net change = -4%.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A data set has mean 12 and sum 72. How many values are in the set?
questions.explanation: Mean = sum/count, so count = sum/mean = 72/12 = 6.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability the sum is 7?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A linear model predicts y = 3x + 10. If the actual value when x = 5 is 23, what is the residual?
questions.explanation: Predicted: y = 3(5) + 10 = 25. Residual = actual - predicted = 23 - 25 = -2.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Machine A produces 100 parts in 4 hours. Machine B produces 150 parts in 5 hours. Which is faster?
questions.explanation: A: 100/4 = 25 parts/hr. B: 150/5 = 30 parts/hr. B is faster.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: If 30% of a number is 45, what is the number?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: What is the median of: 12, 5, 18, 3, 9, 14?

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is P(red or face card)?

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: A poll shows 55% support with margin of error ±3%. What is the confidence interval?
questions.explanation: Confidence interval = 55% ± 3% = 52% to 58%.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A solution is 40% acid. How much pure acid is in 250 mL of solution?

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A stock rises 10% one day and falls 10% the next. Starting at $100, what is the final price?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: If adding a value of 20 to a data set increases the mean, what was the original mean?
questions.explanation: Adding a value higher than the mean increases the mean. So original mean < 20.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: If P(A) = 0.6 and P(A and B) = 0.24, what is P(B|A)?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A correlation coefficient of r = -0.85 indicates:
questions.explanation: r close to -1 indicates a strong negative (inverse) relationship.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Two pipes fill a tank: Pipe A alone takes 4 hours, Pipe B alone takes 6 hours. Together, how long?
questions.explanation: Rate A = 1/4, Rate B = 1/6. Combined = 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12. Time = 12/5 = 2.4 hours.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: After a 15% raise, an employee earns $57,500. What was the original salary?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A data set has Q1 = 25 and Q3 = 45. What is the interquartile range?

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A study finds correlation between ice cream sales and drowning. This likely indicates:
questions.explanation: Both increase in summer due to heat, a confounding variable. Correlation ≠ causation.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: Two independent events have P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.4. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A $500 investment grows to $540 in one year. What is the annual interest rate?

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: The price of a laptop dropped from $1200 to $900. What is the percent decrease?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A regression line has equation y = -2x + 50. What does the slope mean?
questions.choice_a: y decreases by 2 for each unit increase in x
questions.choice_b: y increases by 2 for each unit increase in x
questions.choice_c: x decreases by 2 for each unit increase in y
questions.explanation: The slope -2 means y decreases by 2 for each 1-unit increase in x.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Removing the largest value from a data set will definitely:
questions.explanation: Removing the largest value always decreases the range. It may or may not affect mean/median.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: Increasing sample size will generally:
questions.choice_c: Not affect the margin of error
questions.explanation: Larger samples give more precise estimates, decreasing the margin of error.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: If y is directly proportional to x and y = 12 when x = 4, what is y when x = 7?

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A test has 60% accuracy. If 1000 people take it, about how many get correct results?
questions.explanation: Expected correct = 60% × 1000 = 600.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A store offers 20% off, then an additional 10% off the sale price. What is the total discount?
questions.explanation: Start with 100. After 20% off: 80. After 10% off: 80 × 0.9 = 72. Total discount = 28%.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: An exponential model y = 200(0.85)^t represents decay. What is the percent decrease per unit time?
questions.explanation: 0.85 = 1 - 0.15, so 15% decrease per unit time.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Five test scores have mean 80. If four scores are 75, 82, 78, and 85, what is the fifth?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A tank is 1/3 full. After adding 20 gallons, it becomes 1/2 full. What is the tank's capacity?
questions.explanation: Let capacity = C. 1/2C - 1/3C = 20. (3C - 2C)/6 = 20. C/6 = 20. C = 120 gallons.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A population grows 5% annually for 2 years. What is the total percent increase?
questions.explanation: After 2 years: 1.05² = 1.1025. Total increase = 10.25%.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: The mean of 10 numbers is 50. If one number is changed from 30 to 60, what is the new mean?
questions.explanation: Original sum = 500. Change adds 30 to sum. New sum = 530. New mean = 53.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: Three coins are flipped. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
questions.explanation: Total outcomes = 8. Two heads: HHT, HTH, THH = 3 ways. P = 3/8.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A model y = 500(1.08)^t predicts growth. In how many years will y double?
questions.explanation: Using Rule of 72: 72/8 ≈ 9 years. Or solve 2 = 1.08^t, t = ln(2)/ln(1.08) ≈ 9.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A 40% acid solution is mixed with a 70% solution to get 100mL of 50% solution. How much of the 40% solution?

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: After a 20% discount then 8% tax, the final price is $97.20. What was the original price?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: Two data sets have the same mean. Set A: {3, 5, 7, 9, 11}. Set B: {5, 6, 7, 8, 9}. Which has greater standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Both have mean 7. Set A values are more spread out (range 8 vs 4), so A has greater SD.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: In a class, 60% like math, 50% like science, and 80% like at least one. What percent like both?
questions.explanation: P(M or S) = P(M) + P(S) - P(M and S). 80 = 60 + 50 - P(both). P(both) = 30%.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: A 95% confidence interval is 40% to 52%. What is the sample proportion?
questions.explanation: Sample proportion is the midpoint: (40 + 52)/2 = 46%.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Train A leaves at 60 mph, Train B leaves 1 hour later at 80 mph from the same station. When does B catch A?
questions.explanation: When B catches A: 60(t + 1) = 80t. 60t + 60 = 80t. 60 = 20t. t = 3 hours after B starts.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: If x is increased by 25% then the result is decreased by 20%, the final value equals:

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: If every value in a data set is multiplied by 2, what happens to the standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Multiplying all values by a constant multiplies the SD by the same constant.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. P(both red)?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A linear regression has r² = 0.81. What percentage of variation in y is explained by x?
questions.explanation: r² = 0.81 means 81% of the variation in y is explained by the linear relationship with x.

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: y varies inversely with x². If y = 2 when x = 3, what is y when x = 6?

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A study randomly assigns participants to treatment or control groups. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Random assignment to treatment/control indicates a randomized experiment.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: Company A's revenue is 20% more than Company B's. B's revenue is what percent less than A's?

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: A data set has mean 70 and standard deviation 5. Using the empirical rule, about 95% of data falls between:
questions.explanation: 95% falls within 2 standard deviations: 70 ± 2(5) = 60 to 80.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: A disease affects 1% of population. A test is 95% accurate (for both positive and negative). If positive, what's the probability of having the disease?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: A car averages 30 mpg in city and 40 mpg on highway. Driving 100 miles in each, what is overall mpg?

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: If logarithms of data follow a linear pattern, the original data follows what type of model?
questions.explanation: If log(y) vs x is linear: log(y) = mx + b, then y = 10^(mx+b), an exponential.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: An item's price triples, then is reduced by what percent to return to the original price?
questions.explanation: Original = 100, tripled = 300. To return to 100: decrease = 200/300 = 66.67%.

questions.skill_name: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.question_text: Two polls have same margin of error. Poll A: n=400, Poll B: n=1600. If B's margin is m, what was A's original margin?
questions.explanation: Margin ∝ 1/√n. If n quadruples, margin halves. A's margin = 2 × B's margin.

questions.skill_name: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.question_text: If 5 is added to every value in a data set, what happens to the variance?
questions.explanation: Adding a constant shifts all values but doesn't change spread. Variance unchanged.

questions.skill_name: Probability and conditional probability
questions.question_text: Events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A or B)?

questions.skill_name: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.question_text: Worker A alone takes 6 hours, B alone takes 8 hours. They work together for 2 hours, then A finishes alone. Total time?
questions.explanation: Together 2 hrs: (1/6 + 1/8)×2 = (7/24)×2 = 7/12 done. Remaining: 5/12. A alone: (5/12)/(1/6) = 2.5 hrs. Total = 4.5.

questions.skill_name: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
questions.question_text: A regression equation is y = 2.5x + 10 with r² = 0.64. The standard error is 5. Which statement is false?
questions.choice_a: 64% of variation in y is explained by x
questions.choice_b: The slope indicates y increases 2.5 per unit x
questions.choice_d: The y-intercept has no meaningful interpretation
questions.explanation: The y-intercept (10) may or may not have meaning depending on context. A, B, C are true statements.

questions.skill_name: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.question_text: A survey finds people who exercise more have higher incomes. To claim exercise causes higher income, we would need:
questions.explanation: To establish causation, we need a randomized controlled experiment, not just correlation.

questions.skill_name: Percentages
questions.question_text: A store offers 'buy 2, get 1 free' on $30 items. What is the effective percent discount per item?
questions.explanation: Pay for 2, get 3. Pay $60 for $90 worth. Discount = 30/90 = 33.33%.
